institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try something different. Norway isn't far from Denmark, but Tromsø is all the way up north making the landscape and culture very different from what we know in Denmark. With the Sami as the original population of the northern most areas of Norway and Finnmark, Tromsø was the perfect destination if you are curious about this nomadic people and their lifestyle and culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Go to Tromsø! You will not regret it! It's magical and amazing and I wish I could have stayed for more than one semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. UiT's website provides very thorough information of what you need to have done before arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction meeting over zoom where they gave you all the practical information. Very nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Use Samskipnaden. Sign up in good time, even if you are not yet accepted. I got my housing on pretty much the day of my arrival, but I think that was because I signed up so late. So if you want to avoid being stressed about your housing situation do it in really good time, fx in April. I did it in the end of may/start june.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived at Ørndalen and I loved it. It was a small dorm where I shared kitchen with six people and bathroom with 3. It was nice living with other students and there was a great international environment at Ørndalen, so I can definietly recommend that!

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To be honest I don't quite remember the registration process except that I found it very, very easy and not at all an issue. Once my learning agreement was signed, it was quite easy to registrate my courses. And I think UiT provides very good information on their website and Erasmus/Copenhagen University was also a good help.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UiT' website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do it in good time with the learning agreement.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would describe the level of courses as being a little lower than that of Copenhagen University. I found it easy to keep up with classes even though I did not always read all the texts for the classes. However, the classes were still very interesting!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The same. Seminars and lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SOA-2008: Minorities, Cultures and Human Rights
SOA-1006: Arctic Norway - Aspects of Culture
HIS-1111: Arctic Norway and the Barents region - Aspects of History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
SOA-2008: Minorities, Cultures and Human Rights
This was my absoulte most interesting class! The professor (Hays) was really good and motivating when she gave lectures. It was very interesting to know some more about anthropology's role in connection with human rights.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a great sports and activity organisation called TSI. You can do all sorts of stuff. Surfing, volley, soccer, scuba diving, hiking, etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a great sports and activity organisation called TSI. You can do all sorts of stuff. Surfing, volley, soccer, scuba diving, hiking, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Every Tuesday there is a Cooking Club at the the local Frelsens armee. Even though it's with the church you do not have to believe in God or be Christian to participate. It's an initiative for international students as well as locals to get to together and get to know each other. It's so awesome and I would absolutely reccommend everyone going to Tromsø to go there!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
- Svalbard
- Go hiking as much as possible, especially before the snow arrives
- The climbing centre 
- Go on weekend trip to Senja

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live in a dorm, for example Ørndalen or Dramsvegen panorama. Go to the social activities offered by the host university and get to know people there. There are many great ways to meet people!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Norwegian's tendency to keep to themselves. That was a little sad, but they were nice! They just didnøt seem too interested in hanging out with us.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Brunost and waffles!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Enjoy every minute of it and don't worry about school too much. You will make it ;)
- Engage in social and sports activities 
- Take advantage of the weekends and do small trips in the areas around Tromsø

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: apply for housing as soon as possible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met <3 Exchange is amazing!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid did pose a little bit of challenge, but otherwise not much.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
